channel.title: The Local Europe - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local Europe (thelocal.com)

item.title: Swedish security police justify stance on citizenship transitional rules
item.description: Sweden's Säpo security police has justified its opposition to adding transitional rules to an upcoming bill bringing in stricter citizenship rules, saying that the process of identifying possible threats "often takes a long time".

item.title: PODCAST: The verdict on what the local election results mean for France
item.description: The Talking France podcast returns with a special edition looking at all things local elections - from results and reactions, to what this means for the 2027 presidential election.

item.title: Sweden could start deporting foreigners over 'poor conduct' this summer
item.description: The Swedish government is moving forward with a bill to reject or revoke residency permits of foreigners who are not living up to its standards for good behaviour.

item.title: Swedish Migration Agency works to cut backlog as waiting time passes 1,000 days
item.description: Three months after the Swedish Migration Agency aimed to clear its backlog of four-year-old cases, thousands of applicants from the period are still waiting to be assigned case officers. Åsa Holmes, head of unit for citizenship in Gothenburg, explained the delay in an interview with The Local.

item.title: OPINION: Local elections show French far right is beatable - but not by this squabbling opposition
item.description: This was a Mr Potato Head election - writes John Lichfield - pick different features of the municipal results on Sunday and you can give France the face of your choosing.

item.title: French judge investigates ex-EU border chief for complicity in crimes
item.description: A French judge will investigate claims brought by an NGO that the former head of the European Union border agency, Frontex, was complicit in crimes against humanity, a judicial source told AFP on Tuesday.

item.title: Which countries in Europe have the biggest share of foreign residents?
item.description: In 2025, people born outside the European Union made up about 10 percent of the EU’s 450 million population. But which countries have the largest share of foreign-born residents?

item.title: New Nice mayor poses a 'real problem' for 2030 Winter Olympics
item.description: The 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps, already bedevilled by several senior executives quitting, faces another potential headache with the election of far-right politician Eric Ciotti as mayor of Nice.

item.title: EU says Slovakia cannot charge foreign drivers more for diesel
item.description: Slovakia’s decision to charge foreign drivers more for diesel is illegal under European Union law, the European Commission said on Tuesday.

item.title: Election latest: Denmark set for coalition talks after PM misses out on majority
item.description: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats came out on top in the general election on Tuesday, but neither the left nor right bloc gained an overall majority. That means coalition talks lie ahead.

item.title: Swedish government moves ahead with 'snitch law' bill to track down undocumented migrants
item.description: The government is pushing ahead with a watered-down proposal to make a number of state employees obligated to report foreigners without valid permits to the police.

item.title: ANALYSIS: Five key takeaways from the 2026 Danish election result
item.description: All votes have been counted in the Danish election and the final result has left the red bloc in a slim lead, but with many questions yet to be answered before a new government can take office. Here are five key takeaways from Tuesday's result.

item.title: OPINION: For foreigners in France, each election brings a creeping sense of dread
item.description: The Local France's editor Emma Pearson explains why foreigners in France face an anxious year ahead as the presidential election looms large and the threat from the xenophobic far right grows ever stronger.

item.title: Paris: Hundreds evacuated as fire rips through 5-star Le Bristol hotel
item.description: Hundreds of people were evacuated on Wednesday morning as a fire ripped through one of the French capital's most famous hotels, situated close to the president's Elysée Palace.

item.title: France's Lille to host new EU customs authority
item.description: The northern French city of Lille will host the future European Union customs authority, officials said on Wednesday, as the bloc seeks to stem the flow of cheap Chinese parcel imports.
